name: Thong Yip
description: Pinched golden cups of sweetened egg yolk simmered in fragrant syrup—a royal Thai confection of Portuguese origin.
ingredients: a generous handful of cherry tomatoes
a handful of fresh cilantro, chopped
instructions: Preheat your oven (or set up your steamer or frying station) and lightly grease your pan or molds with neutral vegetable oil.
In a large bowl, whisk together the glutinous rice and red curry paste until evenly combined.
In a separate bowl, blend the fish sauce with the tamarind water until smooth and well incorporated.
Gently fold the wet mixture into the dry ingredients, taking care not to overmix.
Transfer everything to your prepared pan or molds and cook — bake, steam, chill, or fry — until set, about 20 mins.
Remove from the heat and let it cool completely; this helps the texture firm up perfectly.
Garnish with mint or a dusting of roasted peanuts.
tips: For the cleanest slices, chill the finished dessert thoroughly before cutting.
This keeps well for a couple of days in an airtight container, and the flavor often improves overnight.
Resist opening the oven door too early — a sudden change in temperature can cause the dessert to sink or crack.
